title: US GDP Revised Up to 4.3% as Trump Calls Earlier Data 'Fake'
summary: US GDP grew at a 4.3% annual rate in Q3, revised up from 3.4%, as Trump called the earlier data fake and odds of a December Fed rate hike neared 98%.

## Trump Calls Pre-Election GDP Figures "Fake"


In a Truth Social post on Thursday, Trump wrote that "the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE" and asked for "an immediate investigation of this situation," as reported by[Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/trump-demands-probe-pre-election-gdp-data-revision) . "This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error," he added. Fox Business noted that he made the allegation without evidence.


The 3.4% advance estimate was published on Oct. 29, five days before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, in which the Republican Party suffered heavy losses, according to Fox Business. The BEA publishes three scheduled estimates for each quarter, and the agency said the upward revision mainly reflected higher investment and consumer spending as more complete source data came in, Fox Business reported.


## What Does the US GDP Revision Mean for the Fed?


The revised GDP and October inflation data give the Fed reason to lean toward a 25-basis-point rate hike at its Dec. 8-9 meeting, according to[TheStreet](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/fed-rate-hike-bets-deliver-174700533.html) . Per CME FedWatch data cited by Investing.com, the odds of a quarter-point hike in December rose to around 98% after Wednesday's releases, from about 97% before.


The[BEA's October personal income report](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-october-2026) showed the PCE price index up 3.8% from a year earlier and the[core PCE price index up 3.3%](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/gold-price-falls-below-3500-core-pce/) , with both rising 0.3% from September. Core PCE is widely seen as the Fed's preferred[inflation](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-inflation-affects-investing-risk-types-real-returns/) gauge, and it came in above the 3.2% economists had expected, according to Investing.com.


The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4.00% in October after a 25-basis-point hike in September, TheStreet reported. Mike Skordeles, head of U.S. economics at Truist Advisory Services, told TheStreet the data confirm "for us that the Fed will deliver a quarter-point hike in December."


## When Is the Next GDP Estimate?


The BEA will publish its third estimate of third-quarter GDP on Dec. 23, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. EST, the same day as its November personal income and outlays report. Before then, the Fed's rate decision is due at its Dec. 8-9 meeting, per TheStreet.
